rationale: A handful of hyperscalers and labs buy most Data Center output; one buyer pausing or re-sourcing moves revenue by several points, and the same buyers build ASICs, so the risk is correlated with R2 and R7
key_evidence: One direct customer 16% of Q2 FY2027 revenue; H1 FY2027 direct customers 16%/15%/13%; hyperscale ~$48.7B (~55%) of Q2 FY2027 Data Center revenue
leading_indicators: Hyperscale share of Data Center revenue; number and size of >=10% customers in each 10-Q; hyperscaler capex guides
notes: Impact 4 = a 15-30% hit to gross profit if a top buyer cuts or re-sources; likelihood 3 = 30-50% within the horizon

rationale: Every large buyer now has a credible in-house or partner accelerator; ASICs win first on inference cost per token and cap NVIDIA's pricing at the largest accounts
key_evidence: Broadcom AI revenue $16.7B vs NVIDIA Data Center $89.0B (~19%); Anthropic up to 1M TPUs; OpenAI-Broadcom 10 GW; Maia 300 and Trainium4 in 2027; Ironwood ~$1.21 vs B200 ~$1.73 per chip-hour (Est.)
leading_indicators: Broadcom and Marvell AI revenue as % of NVIDIA DC; external TPU deals; NVIDIA gross margin at hyperscale accounts
notes: Highest-likelihood demand risk; already visible in share of growth rather than in NVIDIA's absolute revenue

rationale: Inference is benchmarkable, portable through open serving engines and the natural target for cheaper silicon; token prices fall faster than any hardware cost curve
key_evidence: GPT-3.5-level tokens ~286x cheaper in two years; H100 rentals ~-75% from 2023 peak before a +38% rebound; vLLM and SGLang run on AMD, TPU and others; TPU ~18% cheaper per token than B200 on one workload (Est.)
leading_indicators: GPU rental indices; blended API price per token at fixed capability; inference share of NVIDIA DC revenue; tokens per MW gaps
notes: Impact capped at 3 because rebound in rental prices shows demand elasticity above 1 so far

rationale: Grid connections, not GPUs, set the pace of many builds; the constraint delays revenue and favours the best tokens per MW rather than destroying demand
key_evidence: Grid queues >48 months median; Northern Virginia hookups up to 7 years; ERCOT ~410 GW of large-load requests; PJM capacity price ~11.5x in three auctions; rack power ~600 kW by Kyber
leading_indicators: Interconnection queue times; PJM and ERCOT capacity prices; share of NVIDIA shipments sitting unpowered; behind-the-meter gas permits
notes: Could flip to a tailwind for perf/W leaders; scored on the delay to NVIDIA revenue

rationale: Policy changes every few months and Beijing now steers buyers to domestic chips; China is already small in NVIDIA's revenue and excluded from guidance, so the remaining risk is a protected domestic rival and wider rules
key_evidence: China ~26% of revenue in FY2022 (billing basis), 9.1% in FY2026 and 5.6-8.2% in FY2027 quarters (customer-HQ basis); 25% levy on licensed H200; no H200 revenue recognised; Huawei Ascend roadmap; DeepSeek V4 partly on Ascend
leading_indicators: Licences granted vs revenue recognised; new BIS rules on third countries; Huawei SuperPoD shipments; China share in 10-Q
notes: Impact would rise to 3-4 if controls widened to the Middle East or other large sovereign buyers

rationale: Regulators in China, the US and possibly the EU are looking at NVIDIA's conduct, deals and investments; fines are bounded but behavioural remedies on bundling or allocation could reach the networking attach
key_evidence: SAMR preliminary finding (Sept 2025) with fines of 1-10% of prior-year China sales; DOJ probe and subpoenas (2024); possible EU review and reported DOJ interest in the $12.9B Hugging Face deal; senators questioned the Groq licence structure
leading_indicators: SAMR penalty decision; DOJ second requests on Hugging Face; any remedy touching NVLink/networking bundles or allocation
notes: Customers' alternatives (TPU, Trainium, AMD) weaken a monopolisation case, so R2 partly hedges R6

risk: Circular financing and the capex cycle
rationale: Demand is partly financed by NVIDIA and by credit secured on GPUs; capex cycles turn, and NVIDIA's fixed supply commitments and equity stakes would amplify a downturn
key_evidence: Big-3 hyperscaler capex 4.0x 2022-2026; 2027 forecasts near or above $1T; NVIDIA supply commitments $279B (2.9x quarterly revenue); equity stakes ~$99B; H1 FY2027 equity purchases $42.4B = ~24% of H1 revenue, the same ratio as Lucent's 1999-2000 vendor financing
leading_indicators: Second derivative of hyperscaler capex guides; NVIDIA commitments/revenue; equity purchases/revenue; neocloud financing spreads; rental index
notes: Largest impact score: a revenue decline plus commitment charges plus equity marks hit at once

rationale: All leading-edge NVIDIA GPU dies and all CoWoS packaging sit in Taiwan; a blockade or conflict would halt supply for every AI vendor at once; the chronic version is supplier pricing power
key_evidence: NVIDIA ~60% of 2026 CoWoS wafers (Est.); all CoWoS capacity in Taiwan; Arizona wafers still packaged in Taiwan; TSMC Arizona packaging targeted for 2029; NVIDIA 19% of TSMC 2025 revenue
leading_indicators: Cross-strait military activity; Arizona CoWoS and Amkor timelines; TSMC wafer price rises; memory contract prices
notes: Likelihood 1 for the acute (war/blockade) case; the chronic margin-squeeze case would score about L4 x I2

rationale: UALink, ESUN and Ultra Ethernet turn scale-up and scale-out into multi-vendor markets; NVIDIA's networking (~20% of DC revenue) and its rack-level bundle are what is at stake
key_evidence: UALink 2.0 ratified Apr 2026 with products from 2027; ESUN 1.0 (Mar 2026); UEC 1.1 extends to scale-up (Oct 2026); Ethernet ~2/3 of AI back-end switch sales 1Q26; Helios 3.6 TB/s per GPU vs Rubin 3.0
leading_indicators: UALink switch silicon in volume; Helios deployments; NVIDIA networking revenue growth vs DC compute; NVLink Fusion design wins
notes: Standards are ~2 years behind NVLink; NVLink Fusion converts part of the risk into licensing

rationale: Frameworks, compilers and now AI agents generate the kernels; the long tail of hand-tuned CUDA stops being scarce for the largest buyers
key_evidence: PyTorch in-tree CUDA, ROCm and XPU; Triton on AMD; vLLM plugins for TPU, Gaudi and Ascend; ROCm lag fell to 26 days on DeepSeek-V4; Qualcomm owns Modular/Mojo; agentic RL kernels beat torch.compile on KernelBench (author-reported)
leading_indicators: Day-0 support for new open models on non-NVIDIA hardware; ROCm and TPU share of vLLM/SGLang deployments; frontier-lab silicon mix
notes: Moat already weakest at frontier labs (2.75/5) and strongest in enterprises (4.5/5)
